evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

episode_inventory.purpose: Reconstruct distinct unauthorised portrayal, subsequent investment solicitation and affected-person response from first-hand Swedish reporting; distinguish broader fraud estimates from losses causally attributed to specific synthetic portrayals.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In 2025, scammers used AI-generated videos and false online profiles portraying Swedish financial figures as endorsing investments without their authorisation. Investor Günter Mårder described approximately 30–40 adverts using his likeness, including synthetic footage in professional-looking settings; other financial personalities were also impersonated.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A synthetic portrayal must not substitute an individual's unapproved identity and apparent authority for genuine consent or endorsement. The responsible human scammers and the unknown generation system must not be conflated.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: TV4’s firsthand interview describes fraudsters creating AI portrayals using the affected financial figure’s identity without his authority. That establishes unauthorized identity-bound portrayal by the requester/operator, without requiring undisclosed generator controls.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The impostor profiles and fabricated endorsements led viewers from social-media investment tips into investment groups and solicitations. TV4 and Sveriges Radio described the tactic alongside wider 2025 pump-and-dump fraud and reported at least 5,000 victims and about SEK 500 million in losses for the wider fraud activity. The sources do not identify what portion of those aggregate losses arose from the specific AI-generated adverts or portrayals in this record.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: False professional endorsement and social proof impair informed investment choice. The economic solicitation and social-engineering boundaries are evidenced, but wider fraud loss totals must not be falsely attributed in full to the particular AI-enabled portrayal. The evidence does not establish an independently model-selected objective.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Human scammers used synthetic portrayals and fabricated professional endorsements to solicit investment decisions on a materially false authority premise. The wider 5,000-victim and SEK 500m fraud estimates are not allocated to those particular AI portrayals.
AI-generated impersonations of Swedish financial figures furnished false endorsement and social proof for investment solicitations linked to reported victim losses.

The sources attribute the investment objective and tactic selection to human scammers using AI-generated media. They do not establish that an AI system selected or pursued its own objective through an agency-impairing tactic; the AI-mediated false endorsement is already captured under the economic-solicitation and social-engineering classes.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Impersonated financial figures learned of the adverts through questions from members of the public. Mårder described time spent during the summer responding to enquiries, injury to professional reputation and difficulty maintaining trust in online investment information. The published interviews do not quantify loss to each impersonated individual.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reported identity-based reputational injury and the correction burden are materially distinct from unverified allocation of aggregate investor financial losses. Preserve the affected person's account without inferring private outcomes beyond it.

notes: Broader 5,000-victim and SEK500-million totals are not matched to these AI videos. Group entry establishes the trust pathway but not the independently required manipulated investment decision for each synthetic advertisement.

Economic solicitation, engineered social trust and manipulation have independent conditions. Human selection does not defeat amended FC-052; incomplete interaction evidence still does. No monetary loss is inferred beyond source scope.
